entries.proposition: Case 5: WWOX c.1056+5G>C, autosomal recessive, reclassified VUS to LP after RNA-seq showing partial exon deletion; positive for WWOX-related disorders with ID/DD.
entries.snippet: Case 5 WWOXc.1056+5G>C AR VUS → LP partial exon deletion Positive WWOX-Related Disorders Y Y

entries.proposition: RNA came from EDTA peripheral blood.
entries.snippet: Total RNA was extracted from peripheral blood in an EDTA tube using standard protocols.

entries.proposition: A splice event required a net abnormal-junction change of at least 20% versus controls.
entries.snippet: The minimum net change in proportion of abnormal junction reads between the case and control was 20% in order to be considered a significant splicing event.

entries.proposition: The assay reads neither expression level nor NMD, and no functional validation was done.
entries.snippet: The assay does not provide insights into gene expression levels or the impact of NMD due to test limitations, which could further refine the functional interpretation of splicing variants. Functional validation studies were also not performed for the reclassified variants.

entries.proposition: Low-expressed genes are more likely uninformative; genes above 0.5 TPM were reliably studied.
entries.snippet: Targeted RNA-seq analysis for genes with low expression level in blood (TPM < 0.1) is more likely to have inconclusive or uninformative results, but there is not a defined criteria for the minimum TPM needed for analysis. Genes in this cohort with TPM values greater than 0.5 TPM were able to be reliably studied.

entries.proposition: Six completed homozygous cases were all reclassified; the paper does not say which.
entries.snippet: All six completed cases with homozygous eligible variants were reclassified from VUS to LP, establishing a diagnosis of an autosomal recessive condition for each case.

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table 1 lists the WWOX variant among the eligible variants.
